study_material.title: Geometry - Complete Study Notes
study_material.introduction: Placement geometry sticks to angles, triangles, circles, quadrilaterals and mensuration formulas. It rewards memorised formulas plus a few angle-chasing rules - no proofs required.
learning_objectives: Use angle relationships (complementary, supplementary, triangle sum)
Apply Pythagoras and recognise standard triples
Compute areas and perimeters of standard shapes
Use circle facts (angle in semicircle, circumference, area)

concepts.heading: 1. Angles
concepts.body: Complementary angles sum to 90, supplementary to 180. Vertically opposite angles are equal. A triangle's angles sum to 180; an exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.

concepts.heading: 2. Triangles
concepts.body: Pythagoras: hypotenuse^2 = sum of squares of legs. Standard triples: 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17, 7-24-25 (and their multiples). Area = (1/2) x base x height. Equilateral side a: area = (sqrt3/4)a^2. Isosceles: base angles equal.

concepts.heading: 3. Quadrilaterals
concepts.body: Rectangle: area lb, perimeter 2(l+b), diagonal sqrt(l^2+b^2). Square side a: area a^2, diagonal a sqrt2. Parallelogram: base x height. Rhombus: (1/2) d1 d2 with diagonals bisecting at right angles - side = sqrt((d1/2)^2 + (d2/2)^2). Trapezium: (1/2)(sum of parallel sides) x height.

concepts.heading: 4. Circles
concepts.body: Circumference = 2 pi r, area = pi r^2 (use pi = 22/7 when r is a multiple of 7). Angle in a semicircle is 90 degrees. Equal chords are equidistant from the centre; a radius perpendicular to a chord bisects it.

concepts.heading: 5. Polygons
concepts.body: Sum of interior angles of an n-gon = (n-2) x 180. Each exterior angle of a regular n-gon = 360/n; interior = 180 - 360/n. Regular hexagon: interior 120, exterior 60.

concepts.heading: 6. Solids (Mensuration)
concepts.body: Cube side a: volume a^3, surface 6a^2. Cuboid: lbh and 2(lb+bh+hl). Cylinder: volume pi r^2 h, curved surface 2 pi r h. Sphere: volume (4/3) pi r^3, surface 4 pi r^2. Cone: volume (1/3) pi r^2 h, slant l = sqrt(r^2+h^2).

formulas: Circle: A = pi r^2, C = 2 pi r
shortcut_methods: Spot Pythagorean triples to skip squaring
With r a multiple of 7, use pi = 22/7 for clean numbers
Exterior angles of any convex polygon always total 360
common_mistakes: Using diameter where radius is needed
Mixing up area and perimeter formulas
Forgetting that the rhombus side comes from half-diagonals
study_material.summary: Memorise the formula table, know the special triples and angle rules, and check units - that covers placement geometry.
